audit: Phase B close-out - dynamic attribute access audit (Part 1, item 2)
scope: Every getattr(obj, "field", default) and equivalent dynamic attribute access under src/.
method: Enumerated all getattr() occurrences under src/ at the committed baseline HEAD=212227f: 86 occurrences across 16 files (occurrences, not grep lines -- several lines held two calls).
For each site, introspected the target Pydantic model's model_fields (and properties) to determine whether the named field actually exists.
Where the field exists: replaced dynamic access with direct typed access, handling Optional/None explicitly.
Where the field does NOT exist: the site was provably dead (getattr always returned the default); the dead branch was removed and recorded.
Where dynamic access is genuinely required: left unchanged and recorded with the reason.
Verified with: pytest (386 passed), mypy (no new errors outside inspection/manifest.py line shifts), ruff (no new findings).

totals.note: Counts are getattr() occurrences (not grep lines; several lines contained two calls), measured against the committed baseline HEAD=212227f and recomputed by artifacts/toolchain-validation/closeout/recount_getattr.py.

real_defects_found_and_fixed.root_cause: ObfuscationInspection declares `is_likely_obfuscated` (src/apkforge/inspection/models.py:509). There is no `is_obfuscated` field anywhere in the codebase, so getattr always returned the default False.
real_defects_found_and_fixed.impact: ModificationContext.has_obfuscation() returned False unconditionally, so every modification rule gated on obfuscation was permanently unreachable, regardless of the inspected APK.
real_defects_found_and_fixed.evidence: grep -rn 'is_obfuscated|is_likely_obfuscated' src/ tests/ shows the only producer is inspection/obfuscation.py:183 setting result.is_likely_obfuscated, and the only consumer of the misspelled name was this getattr.

retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.expression: c.get("exported"|"permission"|"name", ...) if isinstance(c, dict) else getattr(c, ..., default)
retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.reason: SecurityEvidenceIndex.has_component_with_names() iterates self.components, and the index's component accessors (services/receivers/providers/activities properties, src/apkforge/security/rules.py:70-83) are deliberately annotated `list[Any]`. The accessor is intentionally tolerant of either mappings or objects. The only in-tree producer (security/engine.py) supplies dicts, and custom rules are declarative YAML/JSON (load_from_directory accepts only .yaml/.yml/.json), so no third-party Python constructs the index today - but tightening this is a rule-engine behaviour change, which this task was explicitly told not to make.
retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.proposed_followup: Tighten the property annotations to list[dict[str, Any]] and drop the object branch (recorded, not done).

retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.reason: Same tolerant-accessor pattern inside has_boot_receiver(), on the same `list[Any]`-typed index data.

retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.expression: s.get("name", "") if isinstance(s, dict) else getattr(s, "name", "")
retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.reason: Reads index.services, the same `list[Any]`-typed evidence-index property.

`modifier` is a plugin satisfying a Protocol, and both sites are inside `except Exception` handlers that report a failure for an object which may be a partially-initialised or third-party modifier. A Protocol attribute is not guaranteed present at runtime on an arbitrary plugin, and raising AttributeError while already handling an exception would mask the original error.
retained_as_genuinely_dynamic.proposed_followup: none - this is the correct construct here

also_converted_after_dependency_check.reason: Initially looked like legitimate third-party version tolerance, but pyproject.toml:35 pins `cryptography>=42.0.0` and the timezone-aware accessors exist on x509.Certificate in that range (verified: hasattr(x509.Certificate, 'not_valid_before_utc') is True). With the floor pinned, the default could only mask a genuine failure, silently recording null certificate validity dates.
also_converted_after_dependency_check.behaviour_change: On the pinned dependency range, none. Below the pin (unsupported), an AttributeError would now surface inside the existing try/except, which already degrades to None and logs.
